newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty drifts sideways, markets await new impetus.
newsitem.headline: Zloty drifts sideways, markets await new impetus.

text.p: The Polish zloty drifted mostly sidways on Monday adjusting to dollar/mark changes but remained basically unchanged against the basket of currencies as foreign investors remained sidelined, dealers said.

They said the zloty would likely remain within its present band between 2.3 and 2.5 percent from the parity rate until foreigners again buy larger amounts of Polish paper, which could come as soon as Wednesday's fixed bond auction.
"The zloty drifted sideways and is likely to continue to do so until the development of a new important factor...perhaps bonds," said Mateusz Bieniek of Societe Generale in Warsaw.
The zloty closed at 2.43/2.36 percent from the trading band centre, virtually flat from Friday's 2.41/2.34 percent close.
It was at 3.0125/45 to the dollar, down from 2.9995/15 on Friday and at 1.8288/02 to the mark, up from 1.8358/73.

Dealers were not moved by a Polish newspaper report, which said Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko was about to leave his post, but said that such a move would destabilise financial markets and could curb the upside potential for the zloty.
"If Kolodko leaves it would increase market uncertainty and zloty gains could be stopped," said Andrzej Kopec, chief dealer at Bank Slaski SA.
On the money market one-day rates increased as a surprising cash outflow left many banks searching for cash at the start of the monthly reserve period, dealers said.
"It seems we had a large cash outflow and it may stay tight for the first part of the week before one-day rates return to around drainage levels," said Malgorzata Sikora of ING Bank.

Overnight rates closed at 22.25/22.45 percent up from 21.65/21.85 at opening. Tomorrow/next were at 22.25/22.45 percent up from 21.75/21.90 percnet, against main reverse repo rate of 21.64 percent for 14-days.
